title: Fixed Three Mirror Channel Cutaway Kaleidoscope
description: One newly authored whole static cutaway kaleidoscope-style display. A finite long outer casing deliberately retains its rear/lower half and both complete annular end collars, exposing two complete long mirror-style plates and the lower half of a deliberately sectioned third plate in a triangular-channel arrangement. The rear end has one genuine small peephole annulus. A separately widened shallow specimen-cell appearance has a complete open front retaining ring, a real half-sectioned wall, an annular rear partition and a low seat containing four fixed coloured solid pieces. Two small attached ground saddles belong to the same display, not a separate stand asset or scene. This is not the tripod telescope without legs or a viewing drum tipped over: all geometry is new, and neither a lens train, pleated camera, upright slit wall nor inner image strip is reused. One prop, zero scenes; specimens are subordinate pieces, not individual models. Five opaque constant PBR roles, metres, Z up and actual horizontal-envelope-centred ground origin. Deliberate pedagogical cutaway: front/upper casing half, upper half of the near mirror plate and transparent specimen cover are not included. Mirror-style panels are opaque illustrative metal, no real pattern, optical transmission, image formation, rotation, calibration, educational efficacy, manufacturing, fit or toy-safety performance claimed.
